    12  # Partitions
    13  
    14  A `Partition` of an element `a` in a complete lattice is an independent family of nontrivial
    15  elements whose supremum is `a`.
    16  
    17  An important special case is where `s : Set α`, where a `Partition s` corresponds to a partition
    18  of the elements of `s` into a family of nonempty sets.
    19  This is equivalent to a transitive and symmetric binary relation `r : α → α → Prop`
    20  where `s` is the set of all `x` for which `r x x`.
    21  
    22  Partitions are ordered by refinement: `P ≤ Q` if every part of `P` is less than or equal to a part
    23  of `Q`.
    24  
    25  ## Main declarations
    26  
    27  * `Partition s`: For `[CompleteLattice α]` and `s : α`, a `Partition s` is an independent
    28    collection of nontrivial elements whose supremum is `s`.
    29  * `Partition.removeBot`: A constructor for `Partition s` that removes `⊥` from a set of parts.
    30  * `Partition.instOrderTop`: `Partition s` has a top element, consisting of just `s` if `s ≠ ⊥` or
    31    nothing otherwise.
    32  * `Partition.instSemilatticeInf`: `Partition s` has finite meets `P ⊓ Q` when `α` is a frame,
    33    given by the collection of all non-bottom infima `p ⊓ q` of parts of the two partitions.
    34  * `Partition.Rel`: The partial equivalence relation induced by a partition of a set.
    35  * `Partition.IsRepFun`: A predicate characterizing a representative function for a partition.
    36  
    37  ## Representative functions (`IsRepFun`)
    38  
    39  `IsRepFun P f` means that `f` sends each element of the support to a representative in its
    40  `Partition.Rel`-class, agrees on related elements, and is the identity outside the support.
    41  
    42  This is useful whenever a construction must pick one distinguished element per part of a partition.
    43  For example, in graph theory one may partition edges into parallel classes or vertices into
    44  connected components; a representative function can specify which edge remains when simplifying
    45  parallel edges, or how supervertices are labeled after contraction. Similar uses arise in matroid
    46  theory and in the definition of minors.
    47  
    48  Tempting alternatives are to use `Classical.choice` or fix a global well-order and take minimal
    49  representatives. However, these lead to issues with inconsistencies: independent choices need not
    50  respect relations between different instances (e.g. monotonicity of simplifications with respect
    51  to subgraph order), a global order can clash with structure already carried by the type, and maps
    52  between different types need not intertwine two separate canonical choices. Stating hypotheses with
    53  `IsRepFun` keeps the chosen representatives explicit; existence under suitable conditions can be
    54  proved separately.
    55  
    56  ## TODO
    57  
    58  * Link this to `Finpartition`.
